topic: NVIDIA-Certified Professional: Agentic AI (NCP-AAI) exam preparation - NVIDIA's newest professional certification for architecting, orchestrating, deploying, and governing production agentic AI and multi-agent LLM systems on the NVIDIA stack
exam_format: 60-70 questions, 120 minutes, online proctored remotely (registration via a Certiverse account). NCP-AAI is a professional-tier credential newly released in 2026. NVIDIA does not publicly publish the passing score or official per-domain percentage weightings, so the domain weights in this course are editorial estimates that reflect the published objective emphasis, not NVIDIA's official figures.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: AI/ML engineers, applied scientists, and LLM application developers building production agentic AI systems. Candidates should have 1-2 years of AI/ML experience and hands-on work with agent frameworks, tool integration, and multi-agent orchestration. A professional step up from the NVIDIA NCA-GENL (Generative AI Associate) and a companion to the NVIDIA NCP-GENL, NCP-AIO, and NCA-AIIO courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Agent Design and Cognition
domains.notes: The core domain. Agent architectures and the anatomy of an LLM agent (perception, reasoning, action, reflection). Reasoning and planning paradigms: ReAct, chain-of-thought and tree-of-thought, self-reflection and self-critique, plan-and-execute vs reactive agents. Roles, personas, and system-prompt design for agents. Structured outputs and function/tool calling schemas. Choosing single-agent vs multi-agent for a described task, and matching the reasoning pattern to the problem. Deterministic vs autonomous control and when to constrain agent freedom.

domains.name: Orchestration and Multi-Agent Systems
domains.notes: Coordinating teams of agents: supervisor/worker, hierarchical, sequential, and collaborative (debate/critique) patterns; task routing, delegation, and handoff; agent-to-agent communication and shared state. Orchestration frameworks and when to use each: LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and the NVIDIA agent tooling (NeMo Agent toolkit / AgentIQ, AI Blueprints). Managing conversation and workflow state, loops and termination conditions, and avoiding runaway or deadlocked agent interactions. Designing a multi-agent system for a described business workflow is the recurring skill.

domains.name: Planning, Memory, and Retrieval
domains.notes: Task decomposition and long-horizon planning so agents keep the original goal across many steps. Memory systems: short-term/working memory, long-term memory, episodic vs semantic memory, and summarization/compaction of context. Retrieval-augmented generation for agents: chunking, embeddings, vector stores, hybrid and re-ranked retrieval, and grounding agent actions in trusted knowledge. Context-window management and cost/latency trade-offs of large contexts vs retrieval. Selecting the right memory and retrieval strategy for a scenario.

domains.name: Tool Integration and Actions
domains.notes: Giving agents the ability to act: tool and API integration, function-calling definitions and schemas, structured argument validation, and returning results into the reasoning loop. Connecting to external systems and data (databases, search, code execution, enterprise APIs) and connector patterns such as the Model Context Protocol. Safe tool execution: sandboxing, permissioning, rate limiting, idempotency, and handling tool errors and retries. Choosing which capabilities to expose as tools and how to constrain them.

domains.name: Deployment, Optimization, and NVIDIA Infrastructure
domains.notes: Serving agentic systems at scale on the NVIDIA stack: NVIDIA NIM microservices for model serving, Triton Inference Server, TensorRT-LLM, and GPU optimization (quantization, batching, KV-cache management) to hit latency and throughput targets. NeMo Guardrails and NeMo Retriever in an agent pipeline. Scaling multi-agent workloads, concurrency, and cost control. Observability and tracing for agents (step traces, token/latency/cost metrics) and debugging non-deterministic agent behavior in production.

domains.name: Governance, Safety, and Evaluation
domains.notes: Evaluating agents: task-completion and trajectory metrics, LLM-as-judge, benchmarking multi-step workflows, and regression testing non-deterministic systems. Guardrails and ethical safeguards: input/output filtering, topical and safety rails, human-in-the-loop approvals for high-risk actions. Agent security: prompt injection and tool-misuse defense, data exfiltration and permission boundaries, auditability. Responsible and compliant deployment of autonomous systems. Choosing the correct guardrail, evaluation, or oversight control for a described risk.

extra_guidance: NCP-AAI is NVIDIA's brand-new (2026) professional Agentic AI certification and the strongest new-trend play in the catalog - agentic and multi-agent AI is the single hottest topic in the market right now, and this is an early-mover professional cert. This course completes the NVIDIA track alongside the existing NCA-GENL (associate), NCA-AIIO, and NCP-AIO courses, and pairs directly with the NCP-GENL course in this batch. CRITICAL accuracy note: NVIDIA does NOT publish official per-domain percentage weightings or the passing score for NCP-AAI, so present the domain NAMES as the exam's objective areas but mark the weights as editorial estimates (they use a leading '~'), never as NVIDIA's official figures - state this in the course where weights appear. The exam is design-and-decision oriented: the real skill is choosing the right agent architecture, orchestration pattern, memory/retrieval strategy, and guardrail for a described production scenario, so practice questions MUST be scenario-based with plausible distractors and 'BEST / MOST reliable / MOST scalable' framing. Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: single-agent vs multi-agent, ReAct vs plan-and-execute, supervisor/worker vs hierarchical vs collaborative orchestration, short-term vs long-term memory, RAG vs long-context, LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen vs NeMo Agent toolkit, human-in-the-loop vs fully autonomous. Anchor the infrastructure content to the NVIDIA stack (NIM, Triton, TensorRT-LLM, NeMo Guardrails/Retriever) since that is the vendor angle. Labs are agent-framework and NVIDIA-tooling walkthroughs at read-and-understand depth (build a ReAct agent, a supervisor multi-agent graph, add a tool, wire NeMo Guardrails), not deep CUDA. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 120-minute time-management strategy for 60-70 questions and guidance on multiple-response elimination. Scan the practice bank for other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
